record.original_question: Let K be a full subcategory of Top0 that contains Sob, is closed with respect to homeomorphisms, and is adequate in the sense that for every T0 space X the space PH(Kdc(X)) is a K-space. Must there exist an irreducible subset system H such that the K-spaces are exactly the H-sober spaces, i.e. K = H-Sob?

evidence.quote: Conversely, for a full subcategory K of Top0 containing Sob, suppose that K is adequate and closed with respect to homeomorphisms. There is a natural question: Is there an R-subset system H such that K = H-Sob? In this paper, we will prove the answer is positive.
K is called adequate if for any T0 space X, PH (Kdc (X)) is a K-space.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. Let $\mathbf{Top}_0$ denote the category of $T_0$ topological spaces with continuous maps, and let $\mathbf{Sob}$ denote its full subcategory of sober spaces. For a $T_0$ space $X$, write $\mathcal{O}(X)$ for its topology and let $\mathrm{Irr}(X)$ denote the set of nonempty irreducible closed subsets of $X$ (a closed set $A$ is irreducible if $A=B\cup C$ with $B,C$ closed implies $A=B$ or $A=C$). 

An assignment $H$ that associates to every $T_0$ space $X$ a collection $H(X)\subseteq 2^X$ of nonempty subsets is called an irreducible subset system (R-subset system) if (i) every $A\in H(X)$ is irreducible in $X$, (ii) $\{x\}\in H(X)$ for every $x\in X$, and (iii) $H$ is preserved by continuous maps in the sense that for any continuous $f:X\to Y$ and $A\in H(X)$, the closure $\overline{f(A)}$ belongs to $H(Y)$ (so that $H$ is functorial in the appropriate sense). 

A $T_0$ space $X$ is called $H$-sober if for every $A\in H(X)$ there exists a unique point $x\in X$ with $\overline{A}=\overline{\{x\}}$. Write $H\text{-}\mathbf{Sob}$ for the full subcategory of $\mathbf{Top}_0$ consisting of all $H$-sober spaces.

For any $T_0$ space $X$, let $K_{dc}(X)$ denote a canonical space built from $X$ associated with the subcategory $K$ (the "$K$-determined closure" construction), and let $P_H(K_{dc}(X))$ denote the natural $H$-indexed space built on $K_{dc}(X)$. A full subcategory $K$ of $\mathbf{Top}_0$ is called adequate if for every $T_0$ space $X$ the space $P_H(K_{dc}(X))$ is again a $K$-space (i.e. an object of $K$).

Question. Let $K$ be a full subcategory of $\mathbf{Top}_0$ such that:
(a) $\mathbf{Sob}\subseteq K$;
(b) $K$ is closed under homeomorphisms;
(c) $K$ is adequate in the sense above.

Must there exist an irreducible subset system $H$ such that $K = H\text{-}\mathbf{Sob}$, i.e. the objects of $K$ are precisely the $H$-sober $T_0$ spaces?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is answered positively in the work that introduces the notion. The authors state that for any full subcategory K of Top0 containing Sob, closed under homeomorphisms, and adequate, there exists an R-subset system H with K = H-Sob, and they prove this. Related literature (e.g., the theory of H-sober spaces and H-sobrifications) supports the framework but the specific characterization theorem is established in this work.

status_evidence.title: On H-sober spaces and H-sobrifications of T0 spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Develops the theory of H-sober spaces for irreducible subset systems H, establishing reflectivity of H-Sob in Top0.
status_evidence.claim: Provides the underlying framework of H-sober spaces and their sobrifications used to formulate the question.

status_evidence.title: On Some Results Related to Sober Spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Studies characterizations of subcategories of Top0 via H-sobriety for irreducible subset systems H.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms that adequate, homeomorphism-closed full subcategories of Top0 containing Sob are characterized as H-Sob for some R-subset system H.
